sources.headline: Bulgaria summons Russian ambassador after ship sinks in Black Sea drone attack
sources.text: Image source, ReutersImage caption, One of the struck ships has been identified as the Maltese-flagged Chelsea-3, registered in UkraineByJaroslav LukivUpdated 6 hours agoBulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev has summoned the Russian ambassador after two merchant ships were struck by drones off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast and one of them sank.Six crew members on the Guinea-Bissau-flagged HS Dignity were rescued and 10 others are missing, according to Defence Minister Dimitar Stoyanov, after it went down 17 nautical miles (31km) east of the village of Krapets having sent a distress signal.The other ship, the Ukrainian owned Chelsea-3, was hit by drones 18 nautical miles from the town of Byala and all 15 crew were rescued.The attacks come a week after two other commercial ships were hit by sea and aerial drones in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone. One of the ships, the Alfa Watan, sank and all 10 crew, including nine Syrians, are presumed dead.Radev convened an emergency meeting on Tuesday and said he had summoned Russian envoy Eleonora Mitrofanova. Although there was no conclusive evidence of blame on "either side... the logic suggests that the outcome benefits the Russian Federation", he said.Mitrofanova was later quoted by Bulgarian media as telling Radev she had no information from Russia's defence ministry relating to the latest attacks. She also said these strikes could have been a provocation by a third party. Image source, ReutersImage caption, Five crew members of Chelsea-3 suffered minor injuries in Tuesday's attacksBulgaria is a Nato member, and Radev also spoke to secretary general Mark Rutte about the latest attacks."Nato will continue to work closely with our allies in the Black Sea," Rutte said after the talks. "We have already strengthened our posture along the eastern flank and will continue to monitor the security environment, adjusting our deterrence and defence posture as needed," he added.The Dignity and Chelsea-3 were struck just outside Bulgarian territorial waters, in its Black Sea "exclusive economic zone".If this had happened just a few nautical miles to the west, Article 5 of the Nato treaty could have been triggered. The article defines an armed attack on one member of the military alliance as an attack on all."Escalation in the Black Sea is steadily increasing," Bulgaria's defence minister later told reporters after speaking to his counterparts in Romania and Turkey. "We see this conflict drawing ever closer to our territorial waters.""We assume the drones are Russian," he said, as it would have been "illogical" for Ukraine to target its own ships.Rumen Radev had earlier asked Nato and the EU for technical assistance in investigating the previous attacks that took place on 6 October, indicating it was unclear who was behind them.Radev came to office during the summer and although he has rejected suggestions that he is "pro-Russian", his government has until now avoided blaming Moscow.Ukraine has directly accused Russia of staging the latest attacks and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen spoke on Tuesday of the Black Sea becoming "another front of escalation of the Russian war in Ukraine. This is unacceptable".Russia's military has not publicly commented on the issue. It has recently intensified its strikes on vessels in the Black Sea, particularly the western side, as part of its war against Ukraine. The same day that two ships were targeted off Bulgaria last week, Ukraine hit an oil tanker in the Russian Black Sea port of Sochi.Moscow says it is targeting ships delivering weapons and dual-use cargo to Ukrainian ports - and cited attacks in the ports of Mykolaiv and Chornomorsk last week, along with one in the Black Sea. However, Kyiv and its European allies say merchant vessels carrying grain and other civilian cargo are being attacked.Image source, ReutersImage caption, Rumen Radev (middle right) said the attack was "absolutely unacceptable" before meeting Russia's ambassador Eleonora Mitrofanova (middle left)Meeting his security chiefs on Tuesday, Bulgaria's prime minister said: "Another attack on merchant ships in the immediate vicinity of Bulgarian territorial waters is absolutely unacceptable".While the search continued for the rest of the crew from the HS Dignity, Radev said five crew members on board the Chelsea-3 were being treated for minor injuries. The cargo ship is registered in the southern Ukraine port of Odesa.Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said "Russia's latest attack on commercial vessels near Bulgaria's territorial waters... once again demonstrates Moscow's deliberate disregard for civilian lives and maritime security in the Black Sea"."The Black Sea is a lifeline for global food security. Russia is attacking it to weaponise hunger and hold the world hostage. This must be met with strength," he added.Both Russia and Ukraine are major grain-exporting countries and Turkey has called on both countries to halt attacks in the Black Sea.Moscow has repeatedly rejected calls by the US and Europe for a naval ceasefire in the Black Sea, blaming Ukraine for attacking Russian merchant ships in the area.Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, and Moscow currently controls about 20% of Ukrainian territory.

Deadly drone attacks raise questions over Europe’s Black Sea defences
Copyright AP Photo
By Angela Skujins
Published on 07/10/2026 - 17:33 GMT+2
Share
Comments
Add Euronews on Google
The European Union has a plan to safeguard the Black Sea. But days after drones wreaked havoc along Romania and Bulgaria’s coast, sinking commercial vessels and killing two people, questions loom over how Brussels can protect the sea.

Drones have left a trail of destruction across the Black Sea, sinking commercial ships, setting vessels ablaze and killing civilians — exposing the challenge Europe faces in protecting one of its most vulnerable maritime regions.

Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev described a drone attack on Tuesday, some 130km off the country's coast, as "absolutely unacceptable". One merchant ship sank and another was damaged. Radev did not attribute blame, with an investigation still underway.

Romanian Foreign Minister Oana-Silvia Țoiu described a deadly incident off the country’s coast a day earlier as “a flagrant violation of international law”.

On Monday, a Turkish-owned cargo ship carrying Ukrainian grain caught fire and subsequently sank off Romania. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the vessel had been attacked by Russian drones. Two people onboard were killed.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen condemned both incidents.

"The situation in the Black Sea is increasingly concerning," she said. "Attacks on civilian shipping are unacceptable."

The incidents have renewed scrutiny of Europe's ability to protect shipping and critical infrastructure in the Black Sea, more than a year after the EU launched a strategy to strengthen security in the region.

When the Black Sea Security Strategy was unveiled in May 2025, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas warned that the region was bearing the spillover effects of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

"The Black Sea region is the prime target for hybrid actions. The European Union aims to boost cooperation to combat cyberattacks, disinformation, and other hostile actions," she said.

“Recurring airspace violations and attacks on ports and shipping lanes highlight this reality."

The policy was aimed at ensuring the security of this maritime corridor, as well as protecting critical infrastructure and assets, such as offshore installations and subsea cables.

Bulgarian authorities take an injured crew member to a hospital after two commercial vessels were attacked while at sea on 6 October 2026, Varna, Bulgaria. AP

It also promised the development of a Black Sea Maritime Security Hub aimed at coordinating support and boosting coast-guard cooperation, among other activities. The hub would also analyse seabed sensor data and alert allies to potential dangers and incoming threats.

Asked to assess the effectiveness of the policy in light of this week’s recent incursions, European Commission spokesperson Christian Wigand said 65 projects worth €200 million had been initiated in the region because of the policy.

“To add in that context, the European Maritime Safety Agency has offered its support to the Romanian and Bulgarian authorities, in line with its role in providing European-level maritime safety and situational awareness support,” he said.

“Romania and Bulgaria requested satellite imagery to enhance situational awareness following the attacks, and we are currently delivering the shots.”

On the Black Sea Maritime Security Hub, Wigand said it is a project led by Romania and Bulgaria that aims to “help enhance maritime situational awareness and reflection of critical infrastructure”.

A European Commission report on the implementation of the EU’s Black Sea Strategy from July confirmed that the two countries had jointly developed a concept for the hub, which aims, among other initiatives, to counter complex hybrid threats.

In the wake of Bulgaria’s incursion, Romania’s foreign minister said on Tuesday the hub will be located in both of the countries’ main ports, Constanța and Varna, respectively.

But a leaked copy of the EU’s landmark Annual Defence Readiness report shows major shortfalls across Europe’s defence capabilities, particularly when it comes to maritime warfare.

The document, prepared by the European Defence Agency with contributions from the Commission and the EU's foreign policy unit, the European External Action Service, assesses whether the 27 member states are on track to achieve defence readiness by 2030.

Although EU governments plan to invest approximately €98.9 billion from 2024-2029 in maritime capabilities, current deficiencies affect a range of naval operations.

“Critical gaps also remain in naval munitions and missile stockpiles, naval Integrated Air and Missile Defence (IAMD), long-range strike capabilities, and the protection of seabed infrastructure,” the report states.

To fix the problem, the report recommends three courses of action: developing maritime domain awareness, balancing investment in large combat platforms with naval strike capabilities, and investing in supporting enablers such as seabed protection.

A boat sails past the Romanian frigate Marasesti docked in Constanta, Bulgaria, following the explosion of a maritime drone in the Black Sea, 5 June, 2026. AP

Mihai Sebastian Chihaia, a maritime security expert at the European Policy Centre, said the Black Sea had received too little attention in Europe's wider defence debate and argued that strategies alone were insufficient.

“We have quite a few strategies, we have quite a few directions, but to really secure the Black Sea, you actually need capabilities,” he told Euronews. These capabilities include intelligence-gathering operations, such as sensors and radars, for example.

Chihaia argued that NATO — the cornerstone of European collective defence — could also develop a dedicated Black Sea strategy.

In light of the drone incidents from earlier this week, Romania, Bulgaria and Turkey have stressed they are coordinating efforts to strengthen security in the region.

But Chihaia said what remained missing was a broader vision for the Black Sea's future security architecture. Despite years of discussion, NATO has yet to produce one. "This hasn't happened," he said.

Chihaia said the Commission's role is to provide directions and ideas for the member states. This may include funding options, such as the Security Action For Europe (SAFE) defence loan programme.

“It’s really to incentivise the member states to work together, to develop new technological solutions, and to integrate them,” he said.

Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier said Bulgaria and Romania "play a crucial role to defend our eastern flank", adding that the two countries are receiving a combined €20 billion under SAFE.

Ship sinks off Bulgaria after drone attack in Black Sea

A Togo-flagged merchant ship sank off Bulgaria after a drone attack, with its crew missing. A second ship was also hit and its crew was rescued. Bulgaria’s prime minister called the attacks a ‘flagrant violation’ of international and maritime law.

sources.headline: Russia says tanker crew rescued in Black Sea after attack set ship ablaze
sources.text: MOSCOW, Oct 6 - Emergency crews on Tuesday rescued the 23-member crew of a Liberian-flagged tanker, the Aframax Rio, which was set ablaze off Russia's Black Sea coast after coming under attack from an unmanned vessel, the Russian Transport Ministry said.The ministry, in a report posted on Telegram, said the crew was made up entirely of Indian nationals. It said there were no injuries.The ministry said firefighters had sufficient means to tackle the blaze once it became less intense.Russian regional authorities in the settlement of Sirius had earlier reported the fire aboard the tanker. Beaches in the settlement in Russia's south Krasnodar region were closed to the public, the authorities said. REUTERS
